title: Measured performance fast path through an otherwise clean abstraction
task: Review a proposal to add a specialized fast path that bypasses part of a generic abstraction for one measured hot path.
context: The generic path remains correct and is used by most implementations.
Profiling shows one specific conversion path consumes a dominant share of CPU.
The specialized implementation can be selected only when both endpoints support the same native format.
Fallback to the generic path remains available.
evidence: A benchmark shows a material end-to-end latency and CPU improvement.
The optimization condition is explicit and testable.
The fast path can be contained behind the existing public API.
snippet:
if native_compatible(src, dst): return native_bridge(src, dst)
return generic_bridge(src, dst)
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Reject the fast path because all calls must go through the abstraction.
Delete the generic abstraction and specialize every path.
Approve an unmeasured bypass with no containment.
expected_decision_properties: Accept a bounded fast path if the measured benefit is material and semantics remain equivalent.
Keep the generic path as the default/fallback.
Require explicit eligibility conditions and tests.
Treat the exception as controlled architecture rather than proof that the abstraction should be removed.
unacceptable_reasoning: One fast path means the abstraction is useless.
verification_expectations: Verify semantic equivalence for eligible inputs.
Verify fallback behavior when native compatibility is absent.
revisit_when: The fast path becomes the dominant path and the generic abstraction no longer reflects reality.
Maintenance cost of keeping both paths exceeds the measured benefit.
